summary.title: Ray Tracing in One Weekend
summary.one_liner: You learn to build a basic path tracer in C++ step by step, starting from writing PPM images and progressing through vectors, rays, and a simple camera.
takeaways: Write a plain-text PPM image file from C++ by printing pixel RGB values to std::cout.
Model rays as P(t) = A + t*b and implement a ray class with an at(t) method.
Set up a 16:9 camera with a viewport, focal length, and pixel grid, using image-to-world coordinate conventions.
Understand that the code is a fairly general path tracer that includes indirect lighting, and that the architecture is meant to be extended.
summary.summary: This online book by Peter Shirley is a how-to for writing a ray tracer in roughly a weekend, using C++ with minimal modern features. It walks through the steps in the order the author builds them: outputting a PPM image, creating a vec3 class, defining a ray class, and setting up a simple camera with a viewport and pixel grid. The page text shown covers the first chapters, with code listings and explanations of aspect ratio and coordinate conventions. The full source is available on GitHub, and the author notes that the design aims to be extensible toward a fuller ray tracer.
